history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN - CSV TOWN CORRECTION: no Vishnupad temple was found in Sangli or Sangli district. The most likely referent is the Vishnupad Temple at Pandharpur, Solapur district (~121 km from Sangli), documented below. The temple stands on the shore of the Chandrabhaga river at Gopalpur, about 5 km from the main Vithoba temple, and is reached by boat across the river (about 30 minutes by boat). Its shrine is a massive open hall supported by sixteen large pillars, housing footprints of Lord Vishnu imprinted in stone in various poses, partially submerged in the river; it is used especially for ancestor rites (pinda daan) and is open on all four sides. The place is quiet and scenic, known for birdlife and sunset views from the river. If the CSV intended a different (small, undocumented) Vishnupad shrine actually in Sangli, this record should be re-mapped. Not to be confused with the famous Vishnupad (Vishnupada) Temple at Gaya, Bihar, where Vishnu subdued Gayasura.

name: Vishnupad Temple, Pandharpur (CSV town Sangli corrected)
town_description: Pandharpur is the great pilgrimage city of the Varkari tradition in Solapur district, Maharashtra, on the Chandrabhaga river; the Vishnupad shrine stands on the riverbank at Gopalpur, a few kilometres from the main Vithoba temple.

travel.airport: Solapur Airport (~75 km); Pune Airport (~210 km)
travel.road: Pandharpur is well connected by road; the Vishnupad shrine is best reached by boat from the main ghat (about 30 minutes)

visitor_information.best_time: October-February; Ashadhi and Kartiki Ekadashi are the biggest pilgrimage periods at Pandharpur
visitor_information.opening_hours: Official visiting hours not published - verify locally before visiting
